_note: One line of plain English for every column in cf/migrations/*.sql. scripts/gen-privacy.mjs renders these on /privacy and FAILS THE BUILD when a column has no line here, or when a line here names a column that no longer exists. Write for the person the row is about, not for an engineer.

columns.users.id: A random account number. Nothing about you is derived from it and nothing about you is stored in it.
columns.users.display_name: A name you typed for yourself, if you chose one. It is never shown to anyone else.
columns.users.email: The address you signed up with, if you chose an address rather than a passkey. No mail is ever sent to it.
columns.users.password_hash: A scrambled form of your password that cannot be turned back into it.
columns.users.password_salt: Random bytes mixed into that scrambling, so two people who chose the same password do not look the same here.
columns.users.recovery_hash: A scrambled form of your ten-word recovery code. We keep no readable copy, so we cannot use it and cannot recover it for you.
columns.users.updated_at: When the account was last changed.
columns.credentials.id: The identifier your passkey handed us when you added it.
columns.credentials.user_id: Which account the passkey belongs to.
columns.credentials.public_key: The public half of your passkey. It can check a signature and nothing else; it cannot unlock anything, here or anywhere.
columns.credentials.counter: A number your passkey increases each time it is used, which is how a cloned key is caught.
columns.credentials.transports: How the key was presented, as your browser reported it: this device, a USB key, a phone.
columns.sessions.id: The random value in the one cookie you get after signing in. It says nothing about you.
columns.sessions.user_id: Which account that cookie signs in.
columns.sessions.expires_at: When the cookie stops working. Signing out deletes the row before then.
columns.journeys.id: A random identifier for a ledger you pressed Save on.
columns.journeys.user_id: The account that saved it, if you were signed in. Blank for an anonymous save, which is the default.
columns.journeys.share_slug: The short code in the link you got back. Anyone holding that link can open the ledger, so treat it as the ledger itself.
columns.journeys.title: The title you typed for the saved ledger, if you typed one.
columns.journeys.entries_json: The units of care, their counts and the short phrases you typed for each line. This is the one place your own words are kept, and only because you pressed Save.
columns.journeys.table_version: Which version of the price table the ledger was priced against, so the figures can be reproduced later.
columns.journeys.delete_hash: A one-way hash of the delete code you were shown once. It cannot be turned back into the code, so the save can be removed by you and not by us.
columns.journeys.expires_at: When an anonymous save stops opening: 180 days from saving. A save on an account has no expiry.
columns.corrections.id: A random row number for the correction.
columns.corrections.price_id: Which published federal figure you marked. The row is about a figure, not about you.
columns.corrections.verdict: Right or wrong, as you pressed it.
columns.corrections.believed_usd: The amount you said you actually paid, if you chose to give one.
columns.corrections.note: What you typed in the box, if you typed anything. It is never published, never exported and never served by any endpoint.
columns.corrections.table_version: Which version of the price table the figure came from when you marked it.
columns.corrections.journey_id: A saved-ledger identifier, only if whoever called the API supplied one. This site never sends it, so it is blank on every row this app has written.
columns.corrections.prev_hash: The hash of the row before yours. This is what makes the public count tamper-evident.
columns.corrections.row_hash: The hash of the published fields of your row, chained to the row before it.
columns.corrections.submitter_hash: A one-way hash of a random identifier your browser keeps to itself, mixed with this one figure. It refuses a second thumb on the same figure and cannot be joined to your answer on any other figure.
columns.corrections.user_id: The account that sent it, and only if you were signed in, so the site can show you what you have sent. Blank on every anonymous send. Deleting your account clears it and leaves the correction counted.
columns.gap_reports.id: A random row number for the report.
columns.gap_reports.counts_json: The counts you entered for care you needed and did not get, by category.
columns.gap_reports.ranking_json: Your ranking of which of those weighed most.
columns.gap_reports.note: An optional note in your own words. Never published, never exported.
columns.gap_reports.context_json: The optional age band, insurance type, region and urbanicity you chose to give. Blank unless you chose them.
columns.gap_reports.table_version: Which version of the price table was live when you sent it.
columns.gap_reports.prev_hash: The hash of the row before yours.
columns.gap_reports.row_hash: The hash of the published fields of your row.
columns.gap_reports.user_id: The account that sent it, only if you were signed in. Blank on every anonymous send.
columns.survey_responses.id: A random row number for the response.
columns.survey_responses.ranking_json: Your ranking of the five burdens, heaviest first.
columns.survey_responses.unasked: Which burden you said nobody ever asked you about.
columns.survey_responses.lead: Which burden you said a tool should lead with.
columns.survey_responses.decide: Who you said should decide how burdens are weighed.
columns.survey_responses.clinicians: How many clinicians you saw before a diagnosis, if you gave a number.
columns.survey_responses.context_json: The optional age band, coverage, region, state and stage you chose to give. Blank unless you chose them, and a count too small to be safe is withheld from the published table.
columns.survey_responses.sentence_enc: One optional sentence in your own words, encrypted with a key kept outside this database. No endpoint serves it and no export carries it; only the number of sentences held is public.
columns.survey_responses.channel: The slug on the link you arrived through, so the sample can be described honestly as what it is.
columns.survey_responses.survey_version: Which version of the instrument you answered.
columns.survey_responses.prev_hash: The hash of the row before yours.
columns.survey_responses.row_hash: The hash of the published fields of your row.
columns.survey_responses.user_id: The account that sent it, only if you were signed in. Blank on every anonymous send.
columns.interviews.id: A random row number for the interview.
columns.interviews.consent: How you said your writing may be used: notes only, quote anonymously, or quote by name.
columns.interviews.name_enc: The name you asked to be quoted under, encrypted at rest. Stored only if you chose to be quoted by name.
columns.interviews.answers_enc: Everything you wrote, encrypted at rest with a key kept outside this database. No endpoint serves it and no export contains it.
columns.interviews.follow_up: Whether you ticked the box asking to hear when there is a new version.
columns.interviews.email_enc: Your address, encrypted at rest, kept only if you ticked that box, and used for nothing else.
columns.interviews.channel: The slug on the link you arrived through.
columns.interviews.prev_hash: The hash of the row before yours, over the four facts we publish about an interview and nothing you wrote.
columns.interviews.row_hash: The hash of those four facts: that an interview arrived, when, under which consent, through which channel.
columns.changes.id: A row number for a change we made because someone told us something.
columns.changes.date: The date we made the change.
columns.changes.said: What a person told us, written in the form they consented to.
columns.changes.changed: What we changed in the product because of it.
columns.changes.who: Who is credited. Anonymous unless the person asked to be named.
columns.changes.source_interview_id: Which interview it came from, so we can find it again. Never published.
columns.changes.published: Whether the entry is shown on the public register.
columns.events.day: The date the count belongs to. Nothing else about that day is kept.
columns.events.name: Which endpoint was called, by its name: corrections, gap, survey, price.
columns.events.count: How many times it was called that day, across everyone. There is no row per person, no address and no session in this table.
columns.integrity_heads.table_name: Which register the head belongs to.
columns.integrity_heads.head_hash: The hash of the newest row, which is the number anyone can recompute for themselves from the published CSV.
columns.integrity_heads.row_count: How many rows that register holds.
columns.agg.kind: Which register the cached total belongs to.
columns.agg.rows_folded: How many rows went into that total, so a total that has fallen behind is spotted and recomputed rather than served.
columns.agg.payload_json: The public totals themselves, exactly as the register already serves them. Counts, never a person.
columns.agg.updated_at: When the total was last recomputed.
columns.canary.id: A random row we write and delete in the same breath to prove the database still accepts writes. It holds nothing else.
columns.canary.at: The moment of that test write.
columns.agg.head_hash: The head of the integrity chain the cached total was folded from, so a total can be checked against the register it claims to describe.
